title: kv-cache: introduce defrag coordinator and adaptive spillover eviction to reduce fragmentation and paging
author: Riley Carter
body:
Motivation: KV cache fragmentation and excessive paging/spillover remain a primary source of tail latency and GPU memory pressure for multi-tenant workloads. Previous PRs improved compaction heuristics, but we still see pathological fragmentation for long-lived keys and heterogeneous sequence lengths. This change introduces a lightweight defrag coordinator that coordinates background compaction, a prioritized adaptive spillover eviction policy, and scheduler hints to reduce interference with continuous batching.

Summary of changes: - New defrag coordinator that tracks fragmentation metrics per shard and schedules compaction tasks during low-latency windows. - Adaptive spillover eviction algorithm that ranks candidates by fragmentation impact, access recency, and estimated restart cost (re-encoding KV segments). - Integration with the request scheduler to add compaction-friendly low-priority slots so continuous batching is not interrupted by compaction I/O. - Kernel hint API: runtime exposes a non-blocking hint so kernels can avoid hot pages during ongoing compaction. - Telemetry: added metrics (kv.defrag_score, kv.spill_candidates_topN, kv.compactions_running, kv.spill_evictions_by_reason) and a dashboard snapshot.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc linked (Linear: ENG-4129) 
- [x] Unit tests for eviction ranking and defrag coordinator logic 
- [x] End-to-end local bench showing reduced paging under synthetic long-lived key workload 
- [x] Observability hooks and dashboards 
- [x] Backwards-compatible: runtime falls back to previous eviction when coordinator disabled

Why this is safe: All compaction work runs off the hot path in background worker threads. The adaptive eviction is a drop-in policy selected by config (default enabled for Dedicated clusters only). Kernel hints are advisory and non-blocking. The change includes feature flags so we can roll out to a small fraction of traffic before enabling globally.

Performance notes: In end-to-end CI bench (multi-tenant mix with 40% long-lived keys): 
- 95p latency for token generation decreased by ~12% 
- Total spillover page writes decreased by ~28% 
- Average memory fragmentation score (internal metric) decreased 40% after 30m of steady-state

See commits and file list for implementation details.

b3c4f21: kv: implement adaptive spillover eviction ranking and unit tests
d4e6b72: runtime: add kernel hint API and scheduler low-priority slots
f5a8c90: telemetry: add kv.defrag_score and spill metrics; dashboard snapshot
9b2f114: tests: e2e bench harness and flaky test fixes
files_changed: telemetry/metrics_registry.rs - new metrics and dashboard config
review_comments: Anika Patel requested changes: please add a safety net to avoid compaction storms when many shards signal high fragmentation simultaneously. Suggest a leaky-bucket rate limiter.
Riley Carter replied: added shard-level token bucket and global concurrency cap in defrag_coordinator.rs; updated tests to simulate burst scenarios.
Marco Ruiz comment: eviction ranking looks good; verify that estimated restart cost calculation uses the new encoding cost model. Left a TODO to validate with real model weights.
Riley Carter reply: incorporated encoding cost model hook; added unit test that mocks encoding time distributions.
Eve Zhang approved: verified metrics and dashboards, tested on Dedicated cluster staging; observed 25-30% reduction in spill writes. Approving to merge.
CI bot: e2e bench showed a flaky test; author re-ran and green - marking as passed.
release_notes: Improved KV cache memory management: introduces background defragmentation coordinator, adaptive spillover eviction prioritization, scheduler integration to reduce compaction impact on continuous batching, and new KV telemetry. Default enabled on Dedicated clusters; configurable via kv.defrag.enabled flag.
